html:
The Zaytuna mosque is the great mosque of the old city of Tunis, founded in the early 700s and rebuilt in the 800s by the Aghlabids. Its school was one of the leading centres of Islamic learning in North Africa.

Scholars there taught law, theology, grammar and science for centuries. Ibn Khaldun studied there, and so did many of Tunisia's later reformers and nationalists, including the poet Abu al-Qasim al-Shabbi.

Under the Hafsids it was at the heart of their capital. After independence Bourguiba cut the school's power and folded it into a state university, as part of his secular reforms. The mosque is still the centre of the medina of Tunis, a World Heritage Site.
